purpose: Futibatinib is used to treat a type of bile duct cancer (called cholangiocarcinoma) that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It is specifically for patients whose cancer has a certain gene change (FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement). It is typically used when at least one other treatment has already been tried.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal protein called FGFR2 that tells them to grow out of control. Futibatinib works like a lock-and-key — it attaches to and blocks that abnormal protein so the cancer cells can no longer get the signal to grow and multiply. This helps slow down or stop the cancer from spreading.
common_side_effects: Nail and skin changes around the nails, dry mouth, fatigue (feeling very tired), diarrhea, nausea, constipation, stomach pain, decreased appetite, dry eyes, hair loss, dry skin, mouth sores, and changes in your blood test results (such as high phosphate levels).
warnings: This medication can cause serious eye problems — tell your doctor right away if you notice any vision changes or eye pain. It can also cause high phosphate levels in your blood, liver problems, and harm to an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is very important for both men and women during treatment. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child while taking this medication. Regular blood tests and eye exams will be needed to monitor for these issues.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 20 mg taken by mouth once a day, every day on a 21-day cycle. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it. Your doctor may lower your dose if you experience certain side effects.
